title: Rachel: Hi Leo, thanks for...
content_text:
Rachel: Hi Leo, thanks for joining! Let's start with a quick intro — tell me a bit about yourself.

Leo: Sure! I'm a software engineer based in China, with about four years of experience building AI-powered products. Most recently I've been working with the Copilot SDK to develop custom AI agents.

Rachel: Oh nice, that's really relevant to what we're doing. What drew you to that area?

Leo: Honestly, I just find it fascinating — the idea that you can give an LLM a set of tools and watch it figure out how to accomplish complex tasks on its own. It's like teaching someone to fish instead of giving them a fish.

Rachel: Ha, I like that analogy. And why are you looking for a remote role specifically?

Leo: I've been working remotely for the past year, and I find I'm actually more productive this way. I can structure my day around deep work blocks instead of office distractions. Plus, I really value the flexibility — it helps me stay sharp and motivated.

Rachel: That resonates with our team culture. We're big believers in asynchronous communication. How do you handle time zone differences?

Leo: I'm used to it. I typically overlap with US hours for a few hours in my evening, and keep the rest of my day for focused coding. I also make sure to over-communicate in writing — detailed PR descriptions, async updates, that kind of thing.

Rachel: Great answer. So what are you looking for in your next role?

Leo: I want to level up my system design skills and work on products that scale globally. Your platform serves millions of users — that's the kind of challenge that gets me excited.

Rachel: Love the energy, Leo. Alright, let me tell you a bit about us...
